rejected.title: The end of feudal privilege
card: Before 1789, peasants owed feudal dues to their lords, such as payments in money or crops and unpaid labour. Nobles and clergy also held privileges, such as exemption from some taxes.
In the summer of 1789, peasants in many regions attacked manor houses and burned records of dues. This panic is called the Great Fear. It pushed the National Constituent Assembly to act.

On the night of 4 August 1789, liberal nobles proposed giving up their dues and privileges, and the Assembly voted to abolish them. Later decrees made some dues payable by buying them out, so peasants did not gain at once in every case.
The decision ended the legal ranks of the old order, where birth gave some people special rights. Careers and taxes were meant to be open to all men by merit.
rejected.remember: In August 1789 the Assembly ended birth-based privilege and feudal dues, under pressure from peasant unrest.

a.q: Why did the Assembly vote to end feudal dues and privileges in August 1789?
opts: Peasant unrest in the countryside pushed it to act
The king ordered it to win the nobles' support
Foreign armies had invaded and demanded reforms
The clergy had already been stripped of their land
a.why: Peasant attacks on manor houses during the Great Fear alarmed the Assembly, and liberal nobles then proposed giving up their dues and privileges. The king did not order the change, and no foreign army was involved in 1789.
a.clue: Think about what peasants were doing in the summer of 1789.

b.q: Before August 1789, Marc, a peasant in Burgundy, paid his lord part of every harvest. After the vote of 4 August, what was the change in principle?
opts: His dues to the lord were abolished by law
His dues went to the state instead of the lord
His lord lost tax exemptions but kept his dues
All his dues ended at once with nothing to pay
b.why: In principle the Assembly abolished feudal dues and noble privileges together, not just one of them, and the dues were ended rather than passed to the state. It is tempting to think every due ended at once for free, but later decrees made some dues payable by buying them out.
b.clue: Separate what the vote said from what peasants had to do later.

b.q: Before August 1789, Marc, a peasant in Burgundy, paid his lord part of every harvest. After the decree of 4 August, what was the most direct change in principle?

problems.detail: Why (a) says the nobles did not ask for the change. On the night of 4 August, liberal nobles such as the Vicomte de Noailles and the Duc d'Aiguillon proposed giving up feudal dues and privileges in the Assembly, so this claim is false.
The right option says peasant unrest 'forced' the Assembly to act, where the card says it 'pushed' the Assembly and the remember line says 'under pressure'. 'Forced' overstates the card.
The right option is the only one with a qualifier and a precise detail ('though buy-outs followed'). It also echoes the card's wording, so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.
